findings.claim: The new pytest imports `yaml` at module level, which reaches the documented local bootstrap-test workflow. That workflow is not a touch point: `docs/developer-guide/testing.md` § The bootstrap script still tells developers to install only pytest, "as CI runs them".
findings.impact: A developer who follows docs/developer-guide/testing.md:78-84 (`pip install pytest` then `python3 -m pytest tests -v`) on an interpreter without PyYAML gets a collection error in tests/test_ci_browser_jobs.py. pytest then reports 'Interrupted: 1 error during collection', so none of the existing configure.py and Dockerfile tests in tests/ run locally. The failure is loud, not silent.
findings.evidence: tests/test_ci_browser_jobs.py:11 `import yaml` (unconditional, by design per spec item 6). docs/developer-guide/testing.md:78-84 says 'Its tests run on a bare interpreter with only pytest installed, as CI runs them: python3 -m pip install pytest / python3 -m pytest tests -v'. ci.yml:494 now installs `pytest PyYAML==6.0.2`. The touch-point list names only the `### Core jobs` table of testing.md, and spec §7 says the rest of the document is unchanged except the Browser suites section.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read-only review). Expected result on an interpreter without PyYAML: `python3 -m pytest tests -v` → ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml' while collecting tests/test_ci_browser_jobs.py, and the run is interrupted.

bucket_proposal.reason: This breaks no declared invariant: I10 concerns CI, where PyYAML is installed. It is an unplanned reach into a documented local workflow outside the touch-point list.

findings.proposed_fix: Add PyYAML==6.0.2 to the install line in testing.md § The bootstrap script and drop 'with only pytest installed', or name that section as a touch point.

findings.claim: The new vitest test frontend/src/__tests__/check-playwright-browsers.test.ts runs in every addon repository's frontend CI and in core's vitest shard, coverage, shuffled and tsc/eslint jobs. The touch-point list does not name this reach, and it goes against a stated repository convention that script checks are scripts, not vitest tests, because core's suite ships into addon pipelines.
findings.impact: After merge to develop, each addon's frontend job (which checks out core develop and runs core's whole suite, testing.md:372-374) also runs this test. It spawns `node` and resolves the installed playwright-core, so a difference in an addon pipeline's install (for example a missing `@playwright/test`) would turn an addon PR red for a core-only CI concern. I found no concrete failure: the test clears PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH and builds its own temporary store.
findings.evidence: frontend/scripts/check-coverage-denominator.mjs:9-10: 'It is a script, not a vitest test: core's suite is executed by the addon repositories' CI, so a new test here ships into their pipelines unannounced.' docs/developer-guide/testing.md:372-374: addon frontend jobs run core's whole suite. vitest.config.ts:13-18 does not exclude src/__tests__, so the file is collected. check-playwright-browsers.test.ts:31-37 and 218-254 resolve @playwright/test → playwright → playwright-core from frontend/. The spec's touch point names only 'A vitest test for it under frontend/src/ (new)', and §7 says 'The other CI jobs are untouched'.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read-only; the addon workflows are not checked out in this worktree, so the addon jobs' install steps could not be read).

bucket_proposal.reason: No declared invariant covers addon pipelines or which vitest jobs collect the test. The spec plans the test file itself, so the issue is only the unlisted reach.

findings.proposed_fix: Name the addon frontend pipelines and core's vitest jobs as places this test reaches, or record why the check-coverage-denominator convention does not apply here.

perspectives.name: scope
perspectives.notes: Every changed file is a listed or implicit touch point. Two behavioural reaches are unlisted: the local bootstrap-test instructions (CD-1) and the addon/core vitest pipelines that collect the new test (CD-2).

perspectives.name: submodules
perspectives.notes: Both browser jobs check out with `submodules: recursive` and run ./setup-addons.sh before installing (ci.yml:313-320, 354-359), matching I5. The new vitest test also runs in addon pipelines, which check out core with submodules (CD-2).

perspectives.name: persistence
perspectives.notes: The old `playwright-Linux-*` cache is no longer written (spec §4 accepts this). The pnpm cache key is unchanged, but the container's store path may differ, which the spec accepts. The vitest test cleans its temp dirs in afterEach. No application data is touched.

perspectives.name: concurrency
perspectives.notes: The component matrix has fail-fast: false. Tests use mkdtemp per case, so shuffled or parallel runs do not collide. The EPUB step runs after a layout failure via !cancelled(). The workflow grows from 14 to 16 jobs, and queueing is out of scope per the spec.
